title: Onboarding failure modes & mitigation — daily runbook
content:
Purpose:
Provide a concise, operational runbook that enumerates observed and anticipated failure modes during customer POC onboarding (private / dedicated / hosted paths), with concrete mitigations, daily tasks for the SE on-call, and an escalation ladder. This is intentionally tactical — use during workshop and first 10 days of customer activation.

Background & context:
- Customer: Acme Financial (regulated data, VPC private control plane).
- POC goal: Integrate Redwood API into Acme's internal ticket-assistant pipeline, sustain 150 qps peak for synthetic load, preserve PII boundaries, and validate canary fallback to smaller quantized model with <150ms p50.
- Deployment mode: Private (VPC) with Dedicated reserve expected to be turned on day 3.
- Current state: infra VPN tunnel established, RBAC keys provisioned, model package v1.2 staged but not yet deployed to customer infra.

Success criteria (customer-agreed):
- End-to-end pipeline sanity: 90% of test prompts return structured JSON (schema v0.3) in first 10s.
- Observability: Traces and token-level cost data visible in console for all test routes.
- Security: No outbound calls from inference instances; KMS-wrapped keys used for secrets.
- Rollout: Canary traffic at 1% for 24h then ramp to 20% with automated rollback on quality drop.

Top failure modes (ranked) + mitigation steps (TL;DR):
1) Model package fails to load under quantized runtime (OOM) — SEVERITY: High
   - Symptoms: large CUDA OOM during startup, repeated container restarts, kernel log shows "alloc failed".
   - Immediate mitigation: reduce batch size and max context via env overrides (BATCH=1, MAX_SEQ=1024), switch to lower-memory quantized artifact (v1.2-q4a) using runtime flag --compat-quantized.
   - Permanent follow-up: add model start smoke test to CI with memory footprint baseline; file JIRA-ENG-1193.

2) VPC peering intermittent drops causing API connections to stall — SEVERITY: High
   - Symptoms: gRPC streams open but stall after prefix tokens, TCP resets observed on edge.
   - Immediate mitigation: fallback routing to hosted API for non-PII test traffic; enable retry-backoff on client (5s -> 20s) and toggle connection pooling to short-lived.
   - Escalation: SRE network lead (Theo Morgan) to open cloud provider ticket; add synthetic heartbeat to detect and auto-failover.

3) Schema regression in structured output (different keys / missing required fields) — SEVERITY: Medium
   - Symptoms: downstream consumer rejects payloads; integration tests fail with validation error.
   - Immediate mitigation: switch to golden prompt set and use output-constrain function-call mode; enable evaluation hook to run post-response schema validation in the console.
   - Permanent follow-up: create prompt-set tied regression alerts under Optimize (linked to Confluence page).

4) KMS integration latency spikes (key unwrap >1s) — SEVERITY: Medium
   - Symptoms: first-token latency elevated, logs show KMS RPCs at 400–800ms.
   - Immediate mitigation: cache unwrapped keys in a short-lived HSM-backed cache per-node (TTL 5m), fall back to local-enc key for non-sensitive tests.
   - Permanent follow-up: coordinate with Security for HSM tuning (JIRA-SEC-287).

5) Canary quality degradation due to quantization artifacts — SEVERITY: Low/Medium
   - Symptoms: BLEU/ROUGE-like metrics drop >5% vs baseline on targeted promptset; customer complains about hallucinations.
   - Immediate mitigation: route 100% of sensitive traffic to unquantized variant; enable reranker post-process with n=4 beam and rerank threshold.
   - Permanent follow-up: run fine-tune or calibration on customer prompts and ship q-config update.

Daily runbook (first 10 days) — tasks for SE assigned to the POC:
- Day 0 (prework): confirm VPN, KMS access, initial model artifacts present, API keys, and console access. Run quick smoke: sample prompts through canary.
- Day 1: full deploy to staging inside customer VPC, enable tracing, run 1k synthetic queries at 5 qps — capture memory/latency profiles.
- Day 2: validate RBAC, secrets rotation, and logging (structured token-level). Begin 1% canary traffic (non-prod).
- Day 3: ramp to Dedicated capacity; monitor GPU allocation and throttles.
- Day 4–5: run customer QA session; collect qualitative flags, map to failure modes; implement immediate fixes for top 2 issues.
- Day 6–7: escalate any persistent infra/network issues; coordinate SRE and Security; prepare for production cutover dry run.
- Day 8–10: production cutover (soft launch) with monitoring and rollback policy active; hold weekly sync with customer PM.

Roles & responsibilities (quick reference):
- Aisha Patel (SE lead): overall POC coordination, deploy oversight, customer workshop lead.
- Marcos Ruiz (SRE): infra, canary routing, autoscaling knobs.
- Lina Chen (Security): KMS/HSM, RBAC review, compliance checklist.
- Theo Morgan (Network SRE): VPC, peering, cloud tickets.
- Customer Eng counterpart: Jane Duarte (Acme) — data owner and acceptance sig-off.

Escalation ladder (who to ping + when):
- 15 min: SE lead (Aisha) and SRE (Marcos) for perf regression >20% or OOM.
- 30 min: add Network SRE (Theo) for connectivity >30 min.
- 60 min: add Security (Lina) for KMS/RBAC incidents.
- 3 hours: involve Engineering on-call (rota) and Solutions Eng manager (Rashmi) for customer-impacting outages.

Risk register (short):
- Risk: Lack of telemetry visibility in customer VPC. Impact: High. Mitigation: partner with customer infra to forward console metrics via secure exporter; if impossible, run mirrored synthetic tests to infer behavior.
- Risk: Customer data classification mismatch (PII in prompts). Impact: High. Mitigation: hold decision with customer legal; route PII prompts to private-only endpoints and mark tests as PII-exempt for hosted fallbacks.

Open questions (to resolve in next workshop):
- Can customer allow temporary hosted fallback for non-PII smoke tests? (Action: Aisha to confirm by 2026-03-11).
- What is the exact SLO for p50/p95 during business hours? Customer has not provided a number.
- Are there existing allowlists for egress IPs? Need for firewall rules.

Meeting notes (workshop 2026-02-27):
- Customer demoed sample prompts and acceptance criteria; aligned on schema v0.3 but flagged two optional fields that Acme wants mandatory.
- Security wants KMS audit log retained for 90 days and signed attestation for HSM usage.
- Agreed to daily 30-min stand for first 5 days.

Immediate next actions (top 5):
1) Aisha: push smoke model start with memory limits to staging and attach logs (today).
2) Marcos: enable synthetic heartbeat and short-lived connection pooling change (today afternoon).
3) Lina: validate KMS wrap/unwrap path and propose caching approach (tomorrow).
4) Theo: open cloud provider network ticket and collect peering debug logs (tomorrow morning).
5) Aisha + Jane (customer): finalize hosted-fallback permission for non-PII testing (due 2026-03-11).

Notes to self (SE):
- Keep the canary small and instrumented; instrument token-level examples for each failure to speed triage.
- When hitting OOM: always collect /metrics, runtime logs, and the exact model artifact sha.
- Draft a short one-pager for customer ops that explains rollback semantics and how to interpret console cost breakdown.

Appendix — quick command cheatsheet:
- Start model with reduced mem: ./deploy.sh --model v1.2 --env BATCH=1 MAX_SEQ=1024 --flags "--compat-quantized"
- Force routed-hosted-fallback (temporary): curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood/fallback -d '{"route":"/ticket-assistant","target":"hosted"}'

Revision history:
- 2026-02-28: created (Aisha)
- 2026-03-02: added network diagnostics and heartbeat plan (Theo)
- 2026-03-10: updated KMS mitigation and daily runbook (Lina)

End of runbook.
